feedback.reason: The checker can require the file and its section labels. It cannot judge whether the prose is true.
A provider instruction on the same line as CLAUDE.md is skipped with the cross-reference. That residual is reviewed, not hidden.
The checker sees the reference. It does not score whether a provider file repeats a rule in different words.
Section labels are checked. Completeness of every command description is editorial.
The absence of a second interface is an analysis of the tree. A new transport would be a new module, which this check does not forbid by name.
The catalog is a runtime registry. Registration completeness is a test, which is the strongest check this layout has.
Ownership is by path. A file added outside the classified set is dropped on init, which is safe and may surprise a new artifact until it is classified.
Python packages are directories. The checker sees the directories, not a build graph.
Import Linter is a linter. Python has no compile-time visibility between these packages.
The entry imports the command layer, and that layer imports argparse. A forbidden-import contract on the entry would treat that intended chain as a violation, so the entry is checked as source text.
Python does not give one distribution a crate boundary inside app.logic. The recorded check is one package. A second package fails the script.
The guarantee is the linter, not the compiler.
The entry is small by inspection of its syntax tree. The checker does not measure what the called command does.
Public-must-not-import-private is a linter contract. The planted fixture tests/fixtures/public_imports_private still uses its own app.private package.
The checker requires the file. It does not judge the importance of each entry.
The words are checked. Faithfulness to the Keep a Changelog categories is editorial.
Unreleased has no date. A released heading with a bad date fails.
The statement is checked. The checker does not parse every version number against the SemVer grammar.
The heading is checked. An empty Unreleased section is still a section.
A git log pasted without commit headings would not match the pattern. The file in this tree is curated.
The link is present. This checkout is local, so the link is the compare shape rather than a fetched page.
Whether a decision can be automated is a judgment. The audit table shows what the gate actually runs.
The ladder is data in the generator. Python does not make the top rung available for imports.
The gap is a sentence in the mapping. The generator requires it. It does not prove the sentence is the real limit.
The table is only as current as the last generate. The drift check is the guard.
Completeness is against the vendored id list. A spec release newer than that file is a drift this checkout must pick up on purpose.
The generator checks that the proof field is present and that the named test exists. It does not re-run every violation test itself.
The signal is automatic. Acting on it, by changing the spec or the tool, is still a separate decision.
Anchors that are shell commands are named, not executed, by the generator. The unit tests execute the checks.
The gate is a local command, not a hosted release pipeline. This checkout is not published.
The report is local. It is not added to the spec aggregator until it is published, which this tree does not do.
The tests cover a nested checkout under app/. They do not prove every future scanner shares the helper.
The split is tested at the renderer. A command that bypasses it is caught by framework/checks/layers.py::direct_writes.
Parser errors before a command resolves stay argparse text. Every command after that uses the renderer.
The envelope is one function. A command that prints its own JSON would be a direct write and fail framework/checks/layers.py::direct_writes.
The audit line stores the rendered text. Commands in this tree do not emit generated artifacts, so the metadata-only case is unused.
The linter sees imports. The script sees print and stdout writes. A write through a renamed builtin is outside both.
The values come from a version file and from git. A dirty tree is reported. It is not compared to a published release.
Test-first order is not recoverable after the files exist. The rule is documented and unenforced. no automated check is named
Statement coverage is the floor. Branch coverage is not configured. The .coveragerc file has no exclude_lines and no omit.
import unittest is the runner and is not a violation. A hand-rolled fake is not a mock generator and is not flagged.
Atomic commits cannot be proven from the current tree. The rule is documented and unenforced. no automated check is named
A network remote that cannot be fetched in a few seconds is reported as unavailable. The notice does not guess a version.
REWRITTEN_NAMES in framework/update.py is empty because this framework does not rewrite paths during an update.
The command renders that dict. A reader still has the prose line as well.
An unknown key fails at load. A dotted TOML key and a quoted key both name the same option.
